title: Pin the project-level .omp directory to its own constant, never renamed
one_line: Split the project-root directory name out of CONFIG_DIR_NAME into a deliberately-never-renamed PROJECT_DIR_NAME, and repoint every project-level call site at it, so that flipping the home config root in W6 cannot silently stop a user's committed .omp/ directory from being read.
user_visible_effect: Nothing changes on screen during M5, and that is the point: every project that has a .omp directory — including this repository's own, which holds 14 git-tracked files under .omp/commands, .omp/skills and .omp/tools — keeps resolving to that exact directory after the home config root moves to ~/.ultraworkers. The rules editor still shows the scope label 'This project (.omp/rules)'. What the user never sees is the failure this work item exists to prevent: no error, no warning, no missing-config message, just project settings, rules, skills, hooks, extensions, MCP and SSH config silently vanishing from every repo they have been working in, followed by a silent re-login because the app now believes it is freshly installed.

test_contract: Defends one thing, stated as an observable contract: the project-level config directory name is a DIFFERENT identity from the home-level one, and it is pinned. Two assertions carry the weight. (1) DIVERGENCE: PROJECT_DIR_NAME !== CONFIG_DIR_NAME. This is the assertion that matters most and it has no counterpart anywhere in the existing suite — every existing test asserts a specific value, and a specific value is satisfied by a constant that is accidentally still coupled. Divergence is only false when someone has re-merged the two, which is precisely the mistake. What the consumer sees if this regresses: a user opens a repo they have been using for months and their project settings, rules, skills and hooks are gone; no error is printed, no missing-config warning appears, and the app behaves as if freshly installed — including a silent re-login, because the app's own identity state resolves as new. (2) RESOLUTION UNDER ADVERSARY: a temp cwd containing a committed .omp/ still resolves there when a directory named after the NEW home root sits right next to it. This is a real resolution, not a string comparison — getProjectAgentDir is called and its return value compared. A test that only asserted the string ".omp" would pass even if the function were never called. The secondary contract is that the five project getters in dirs.ts built on getProjectAgentDir (getProjectModulesDir, getProjectPromptsDir, getProjectPluginOverridesPath, getMCPConfigPath('project'), getSSHConfigPath('project')) all land under the pinned .omp — if that regresses, project-local modules, prompts, plugin overrides, MCP servers and SSH config silently resolve to a directory that does not exist. The pre-existing tests are the negative controls and must NOT be edited: omfg-controller.test.ts hard-codes 'This project (.omp/rules)' at line 15 and the literal <projectDir>/.omp/rules paths at 178 and 198; agent-session-rules-reload.test.ts hard-codes <tempDir>/.omp/RULES.md at line 89 and .omp/rules at 156; advisor-toggle.test.ts and extensions-discovery.test.ts build project paths through getProjectAgentDir. If the repointing in steps 3-4 is skipped, these go red — that is what makes them the real evidence rather than the new test. NOT source-grep: the new test imports and calls the real functions and compares real resolved paths. NOT mock.module(): the seam is narrower and better — getProjectAgentDir already takes cwd as a parameter, so no global state is touched at all.

W5 — HARD GATE. `config migrate` is the user's manual path back. W6a deliberately does NOT extend it to the project root (option b), so W5 must ship with its scope clearly limited to the two home roots, or the two will disagree about what 'migrated' means.

W7 — the do_not_rename row created in step 8 is part of the exclusion list W7's 4107-file sed loads

effort: S by the plan's grading, but larger than the plan's own description of 'a separate constant, one do_not_rename line, one test case'. Real count, all verified: 1 new constant, 4 call sites repointed (only 1 of which the plan names — dirs.ts:590, discovery/helpers.ts:47, omfg-controller.ts:285, plus the config.ts:12 decision), 1 test file created, 1 line of an existing test relaxed, 1 do_not_rename row. The gap between 'S' and what S actually contains here is the two unnamed call sites. Option (a) from the plan — dual-read at the project level — remains M and is NOT recommended; it would force `config migrate` to touch a directory that is committed to the user's git history, which is the one thing this milestone is chartered not to do.
risk: The single most likely failure is believing the plan's framing that W6a is one line at dirs.ts:590, and leaving discovery/helpers.ts:47 and omfg-controller.ts:285 reading CONFIG_DIR_NAME. Both were found by running the grep the plan does not run, and both fail in the same silent way: project-scope rules resolve to an empty directory and project-local skills, commands, agents and hooks discovery returns nothing — no error, no missing-config warning, and the rules editor's own label still reads 'This project (.omp/rules)' while pointing at a directory that does not exist. That last detail is what makes it nasty: the UI confirms the wrong location. Second risk is the config.ts:12 priorityList decision (open question 1) being made by whoever is editing fastest rather than by a product decision, because it determines whether project-level config keeps reading .omp or silently starts reading .ultraworkers, and getting it wrong looks exactly like doing nothing. Third risk is treating the divergence assertion as redundant because the value assertion already pins '.omp' — they are not redundant, and clause (3) of the gate exists specifically to prove that. Fourth is the keep-list entry landing without a reason, which makes it unreviewable and defeats the entire purpose of the file W7 depends on. Fifth, and structural: the repo's OWN .omp/ is committed with 14 tracked files (.omp/commands/*.md x5, .omp/skills/** x6, .omp/tools/** x3), so this is not a hypothetical for this codebase — flipping the project root would break this repository's own commands and skills on the maintainer's machine.
open_questions: 1. BLOCKING — packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:12. priorityList feeds BOTH USER_CONFIG_BASES (line 84) and PROJECT_CONFIG_BASES (line 90) from the same `dir` value, and line 135 compares `name !== CONFIG_DIR_NAME` to decide user-source opt-in. If PROJECT_DIR_NAME is introduced and this file is untouched, the project entry in PROJECT_CONFIG_BASES silently becomes '.ultraworkers' — a project-level behaviour change hiding inside a constant rename. Recommendation: switch that one priorityList entry to PROJECT_DIR_NAME so project config keeps reading the committed .omp. This is a product decision (does the user's repo keep its committed .omp?) and must be answered by a person before merge, not inferred by the implementer. Affects: getConfigDirs('skills'|'commands'|'agents'|'hooks', {level:'project'}) and every project-level config lookup routed through it.

2. NON-BLOCKING — should the do_not_rename row for the project .omp be created by this work item or left to whichever item first creates scripts/rename/keep-list.txt? Verified: scripts/rename/ does not exist on HEAD 84cbac9, so somebody has to create it. Plan section 2.3 assigns the file to the milestone, W7 gates on it, and section 2.3's format requires a mandatory '#' reason per entry. Recommendation: W6a creates it with the single project-.omp row, appending rather than overwriting if a sibling got there first.

3. NON-BLOCKING — is a permanent divergence (CONFIG_DIR_NAME = '.ultraworkers', PROJECT_DIR_NAME = '.omp', forever) acceptable as a shipped end state, or does it need a dated follow-up? The plan's option (b) is a keep-forever decision and N14 records it as such. Worth a maintainer's explicit acknowledgement because the codebase will permanently carry two directory names, and the next person to read dirs.ts:27-40 will ask why.

4. NON-BLOCKING, environment — the coding-agent negative controls (omfg-controller.test.ts, extensions-discovery.test.ts) cannot run on this machine without `brew install ninja` followed by `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`. Should the milestone's verification environment be provisioned once so the whole negative-control set becomes runnable, or should each spec keep declaring which of its gates are locally unrunnable? Recommend the former: the blocker has now cost every work item in this milestone a caveat, and a working addon would let the strongest signals actually fire.

plan_corrections.correction: The line number, the direct read, and the W4/W5/W6 blindness are all verified exactly: dirs.ts:590 is `return path.join(cwd, CONFIG_DIR_NAME);` and `grep -n CONFIG_DIR_NAME packages/utils/src/dirs.ts` returns exactly 3 hits (27, 298, 590). What the plan misses is that dirs.ts:590 is only ONE of three project-level reads. `git grep -n CONFIG_DIR_NAME -- '*.ts' ':!*test*'` returns two more project-root joins outside dirs.ts: packages/coding-agent/src/discovery/helpers.ts:47 (`projectDir: CONFIG_DIR_NAME`, consumed by getProjectPath() at :127-131 as path.join(ctx.cwd, paths.projectDir, subpath)) and packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/omfg-controller.ts:285 (project-scope rules write path). Neither goes through getProjectAgentDir(), so neither is covered by repointing line 590, and the plan's W6a text names neither.
